candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record describes angiofibromas in a patient with prior renal transplant (consistent with nephropathic cystinosis) and electron microscopy showing crystalline inclusions within fibroblast lysosomes — the hallmark of cystinosis. The reference diagnosis is cutaneous cystinosis, meaning cystine crystal deposition in the skin causing the angiofibromatous papules. TSC is a plausible differential given the angiofibromas and conical teeth, but the absence of other TSC stigmata (hypopigmented macules, periungual fibromas, Shagreen plaques) and the definitive EM finding of crystalline lysosomal inclusions point away from TSC. C001 asserts an incompatible etiology (TSC genetic hamartoma syndrome) rather than the correct diagnosis of cutaneous cystinosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: TSC-associated angiofibromas is a related but distinct diagnosis; the reference requires cutaneous cystinosis as the underlying etiology of the angiofibromas

case_quality_flags: Electron microscopy finding of crystalline lysosomal inclusions is pathognomonic for cystinosis and decisively excludes TSC as the primary diagnosis
Renal transplant history at age 14 strongly supports nephropathic cystinosis with subsequent cutaneous manifestation
